reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a PancakeSwap bot with claims of easy 10x daily returns and up to roughly 1,000 BNB per day. It instructs viewers to deposit BNB into the contract and activate it, while the stated recovery method requires an additional BNB transfer before the earlier deposit can be returned.

citations.quote: FREE PancakeSwap Bot | EASY 10x profit EVERY DAY
Deposit funds to exact your newly BOT contract address
After the transaction is confirmed, Start the BOT by clicking the "Action" button
it will automatically sell within a minute
so that way it will front run all the retail uh investors that come in

opening.argument: Judge, the description explicitly warns that imitation contracts can put funds at risk and recommends precautions before using the code. It also addresses the possibility that the contract generates no revenue and describes a withdrawal procedure. Those passages do not prove the procedure works, but they complicate the reading that this is simply an unconditional promise of profit. The speaker presents a technical process with stated limitations, including a minimum funding threshold, rather than claiming every deposit will immediately earn a return.

citations.quote: If you are fooled by other contracts that imitate my clip robot, for the safety of funds, it is best to create a new wallet and delete the browser browsing history (cookie) before using the code
Q3: What should I do if there is no revenue generated after the contract runs?
The main reason is that there are less funds deposited. In order to ensure the hit rate, the contract will temporarily refuse the transaction until the required amount is reached.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title's return claim is aggressive, but the opening treats it as though it exhausts the video's message. The description also contemplates no revenue and tells viewers they can seek withdrawal. Likewise, instructions to fund and activate a contract establish what the presenter wants viewers to do, not that the presenter controls the resulting funds or that a return is fabricated. The cited front-running explanation describes the proposed trading behavior; by itself it does not establish deception.

citations.quote: You can choose to refer to Q1 to withdraw funds or add at least 1 BNB.
so that way it will front run all the retail uh investors that come in

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning concerns imitation contracts, not the risks of this bot's claimed returns. The no-revenue answer directs viewers toward adding funds, while the stated withdrawal procedure requires another transfer equal to the original deposit. Those details reinforce the concern created by the daily-profit pitch and funding instructions; they do not substantiate a working safeguard.

citations.quote: If you are fooled by other contracts that imitate my clip robot
when you need to return the funds, you need to transfer 1.0 BNB to the contract, and then action
FREE PancakeSwap Bot | EASY 10x profit EVERY DAY

opening.argument: Judge, much of the presentation is a step-by-step contract walkthrough. The speaker explains creating a file in Remix, compiling the contract, connecting a wallet, deploying, and looking up the resulting address on BscScan. He also discusses the intended router interaction and timing of buys and sells. That is concrete technical instruction, not merely a demand to send money to an unexplained destination. His reported profits should be read as a personal claim made during the demonstration, not independent proof that another viewer will obtain the same result.

citations.quote: Under contracts I'm going to create a new contract which is with this new file create new file icon on the top left.
There we go. It compiled. So we're gonna do injected web3 Make sure that your wallet is connected to remix
I copy and paste that into BSEscan. You can see through there is an address for that.
I've had really good luck with this the last few weeks I've made you know several hundred B and B, which I can show the transaction reports on bsc scan to corroborate that

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies funding and activation steps, but those steps also belong to the contract demonstration it quotes. The speaker says he funds the contract he has just created and then presses its action button. Even the one-minute sale and retail front-running passages explain the behavior he claims the program performs. They do not, on their own, verify that the program works, but neither do they establish that the walkthrough is a disguised transfer to the presenter.

citations.quote: so we're gonna send some funds to that contract that we just created
the action button then engages all the constructors that i built in as far as engaging the pancake router uh it automatically buys and sells for you

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can still solicit deposits through a claimed profit mechanism. The description instructs viewers to paste supplied contract code, deposit funds, and activate it; the speaker then claims a rapid return. Showing deployment steps or an address lookup does not verify the code's behavior, the ownership of funds after transfer, or the claimed profits.

citations.quote: Paste SmartContract in Remix: (Copy and Paste as it is)
Deposit funds to exact your newly BOT contract address
and there we go yeah it's already is around 15x

opening.argument: Judge, the proposed transaction is presented as using a self-deployed trading contract, not buying access from a seller. The instructions route viewers through MetaMask and Remix, say the deployed bot is their own, and describe returns as coming from automated trades. The supplied account does not identify a payment to the presenter, a recruitment commission, or a request to hand over wallet credentials. The large earnings claims deserve skepticism, and the contract has not been independently validated here, but skepticism about a product claim is not itself proof that the presenter receives viewers' deposits.

citations.quote: Access Remix: https://remix.ethereum.org
After the transaction is confirmed, it's your own BOT now
Deposit funds to exact your newly BOT contract address
it automatically buys and sells for you

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that viewers are instructed to deposit BNB; that is a material risk, not something to overlook. But its opening does not identify where the deposited BNB ultimately goes or establish that the presenter receives it. The FAQ's additional-transfer instruction is troubling, yet it is stated as a refund method, not shown as a completed loss. The title and profit estimates are promotional claims, not verification of either genuine returns or diversion of funds.

citations.quote: Q1: How to return the BNB deposited in the contract?
you need to transfer 1.0 BNB to the contract, and then action
EASY 10x profit EVERY DAY

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the contract the viewer's own does not establish control over its funds, particularly when viewers are told to paste supplied code. The mechanism does require a deposit, advertises extraordinary returns, and says that recovering an earlier deposit requires sending the same amount again. The absence of a shown presenter payout does not neutralize that combination of solicitation and escalating payment demands.
